chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Your motorcycle is fully loaded. How do you drive down a long mountain pass road?

options.text: Utilize the braking effect of the engine by changing to a lower gear
Do not drive too fast between bends in order to avoid overheating the brakes
Use the front wheel brake only

correct_answers.text: Utilize the braking effect of the engine by changing to a lower gear
Do not drive too fast between bends in order to avoid overheating the brakes

comment: When driving down over a long period of time, your brakes are at risk to overheat. To avoid this, try to use the braking effect of the engine on a low gear and limit the acceleration/deceleration in between turns.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: When is there a danger of the motorcycle's front wheel lifting off the road?

options.text: On rapid acceleration in low gear
If the clutch is suddenly released on starting off
When the handbrake is pulled on hard

correct_answers.text: On rapid acceleration in low gear
If the clutch is suddenly released on starting off

comment: Fast and sudden accelerations could lead to the front wheel lifting off the road. This could happen when accelerating on low gear or releasing the clutch suddenly when starting to drive

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You have changed the motorcycle. For the first time, you are driving a motorcycle with fairings. What is different?

options.text: As the wind pressure is reduced, there is a tendency to drive faster
Sensitivity to side wind increases
The danger of falling has decreased

correct_answers.text: As the wind pressure is reduced, there is a tendency to drive faster
Sensitivity to side wind increases

comment: Fairings do not decrease the danger of falling. However, it increases the sensitivity to the side wind but diminishes the front wind which creates a tendency to drive faster

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you particularly remember when carrying side-mounted cases or bags?

options.text: To avoid an uneven distribution of weight
Not to exceed the top speed recommended by the manufacturer of the motorcycle
With a full load, apply the rear brakes only

correct_answers.text: To avoid an uneven distribution of weight
Not to exceed the top speed recommended by the manufacturer of the motorcycle

comment: Adding luggage to your motorcycle will impact its behavior on the road. Make sure you do not exceed the maximum speed recommended by your manufacturer for driving with luggage and that you distribute weight evenly (on the right and left) to keep your motorcycle stable

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What happens if you engage too low a gear and quickly release the clutch when driving at high speed?

options.text: The rear wheel locks and can slip sideways
A fall is often unavoidable
The front wheel lifts off the ground

correct_answers.text: The rear wheel locks and can slip sideways
A fall is often unavoidable

comment: If you engage a gear that is too low and release the clutch, your motorcycle will brutally decelerate and could cause you to fall or slip sideways

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you check on your motorcycle before you set off?

options.text: The adjustment of the rear-view mirrors
Brake fluid level, lever travel
Setting of the camshaft

correct_answers.text: The adjustment of the rear-view mirrors
Brake fluid level, lever travel

comment: Before starting to drive, make sure that the rearview mirrors are correctly installed, adjusted and work properly (not broken, blind) and that the breaks work properly

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: When do you have to increase tyre pressure?

options.text: When you have a passenger
When driving on autobahns for longer periods of time at high speed
When driving with heavy luggage

correct_answers.text: When you have a passenger
When driving on autobahns for longer periods of time at high speed
When driving with heavy luggage

comment: Tire pressure need to be increased if driving with more weight (additional passenger, heavy luggage) or when driving for long distances especially at high speed

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you remember when taking a passenger?

options.text: Driving characteristics change on bends, particularly when entering and leaving the bend
Under the same conditions, overtaking requires a longer distance
Under the same conditions, the braking distance is reduced

correct_answers.text: Driving characteristics change on bends, particularly when entering and leaving the bend
Under the same conditions, overtaking requires a longer distance

comment: A passenger increases the weight on your motorcycle. This makes accelerating and thus overtaking longer. It increases the centrifugal force when turning and increases the braking distance.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you do to be ready to brake?

options.text: Place your hand on the handbrake lever
Position your foot over the brake pedal
Change to a higher gear

correct_answers.text: Place your hand on the handbrake lever
Position your foot over the brake pedal

comment: By placing your hand on the handbrakes and foot over the brake pedal you improve your reaction time to break

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Why does the rear wheel of a motorcycle tend to lock when braking rather than the front wheel?

options.text: - the load on the rear wheel is reduced
- the rear wheel is still propelled
- the load on the rear wheel increases

correct_answers.text: - the load on the rear wheel is reduced

comment: When breaking, more weight is applied on the front wheel and less on the back wheel which can lock the back wheel

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What is correct when driving round bends on downhill slopes?

options.text: Brake adequately before the bend so that no additional braking is needed on the bend
Start taking the bend so that you do not get into the area of oncoming traffic even when you are leaning far over
When you do not see any oncoming traffic, follow the ideal line and use the whole width of the roadway

correct_answers.text: Brake adequately before the bend so that no additional braking is needed on the bend
Start taking the bend so that you do not get into the area of oncoming traffic even when you are leaning far over

comment: When going downhill you need to break more than on bends on flat areas. You should therefore break enough before the bend, you should also keep your distance from the demarcation line from the oncoming traffic in case you need to tilt your motorcycle more

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving round a bend at a brisk pace which is tighter than you first thought. What do you do?

options.text: Throttle back, lean further over
Do not brake sharply
Make an immediate sharp steering movement

correct_answers.text: Throttle back, lean further over
Do not brake sharply

comment: In this situation, making a sharp steering movement will be dangerous and could lead to a fall. You should decelerate gradually and lean further to turn more. If you brake sharply while turning, a torque force would tilt you from leaning to one side to a more upward position which will increase the radius of your turn

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you particularly remember when raising motorcycles onto their stands (centre stands)?

options.text: - must be hard and even
- should not slope steeply downwards
- must not slope upwards

correct_answers.text: - must be hard and even
- should not slope steeply downwards

comment: To avoid the motorcycle to tip over or fall, you must ensure that the ground is firm, even and not too steep on a downward slope

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Why is the rule of having to adapt your driving to your visibility particularly important in bends?

options.text: Because bends can be tighter than expected
Because dangerously soiled roadways may be recognized too late
Because otherwise you lose too much momentum

correct_answers.text: Because bends can be tighter than expected
Because dangerously soiled roadways may be recognized too late

comment: In a bend, there is limited visibility due to the curvature of the road. You should reduce your speed as unforeseen risk factors such as dirt on the road, obstacles or tighter bends could appear

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: How can you counteract centrifugal force?

options.text: By leaning over
By reducing speed
By accelerating rapidly

correct_answers.text: By leaning over
By reducing speed

comment: The centrifugal force can be either reduced by driving at a slower speed or be counteracted by leaning over more. Accelerating will do the opposite and increase the centrifugal force

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can happen if a motorcycle is accelerated rapidly?

options.text: If turning left, the motorcycle could leave the roadway and endanger pedestrians on the pavement
If turning right, the motorcycle can veer into the path of oncoming traffic
If driving straight ahead, driving stability is increased in any case

correct_answers.text: If turning left, the motorcycle could leave the roadway and endanger pedestrians on the pavement
If turning right, the motorcycle can veer into the path of oncoming traffic

comment: Accelerating while turning will increase the centrifugal force which will increase the radius of your turn. This could result in being directed in incoming traffic or on the pavement. In a straight line accelerating rapidly decrease stability

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must be changed before driving with a heavy load?

options.text: Pre-tensioning of the springs
Tyre pressure
Chain tension

correct_answers.text: Pre-tensioning of the springs
Tyre pressure

comment: When driving with heavy loads, make sure to increase the tire pressure and adjust the pre-tension in the suspension springs

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Which checks are particularly important before setting off?

options.text: Profile of the rear tyre
Even load (front/rear, right/left)
Condition of your visor

correct_answers.text: Profile of the rear tyre
Even load (front/rear, right/left)
Condition of your visor

comment: All three are important to check before starting to drive. Make sure your visor is in good condition and not damaged or scratched. If you carry weight, make sure it is evenly distributed to not impact your center of gravity and do not impact your stability. Also ensure that the rear tire is in good condition.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: In which cases should you apply the brakes only very carefully?

options.text: On roadways with loose chippings or sand
On tram tracks, sewer covers and lane markings
When driving for the first time with new tyres

correct_answers.text: On roadways with loose chippings or sand
On tram tracks, sewer covers and lane markings
When driving for the first time with new tyres

comment: You should break carefully on slippery surfaces such as wet roads, tram tracks, sewer covers, lane markings but also dirt roads, roads with sand, stones as well as when driving with new tires

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What is the normal braking procedure for motorcycles?

options.text: Applying both brakes
Applying the rear brake only
Applying the front brake only

correct_answers.text: Applying both brakes

comment: You should apply both brakes which will result in a shorter stopping distance than only applying one of the breaks

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Why must both brakes on a motorcycle always be in perfect working order?

options.text: To achieve the shortest possible braking distance
To be able to brake if one of the brakes fails
To safely park the motorcycle on a downhill slope

correct_answers.text: To achieve the shortest possible braking distance
To be able to brake if one of the brakes fails

comment: Both brakes are required to function in case one of them suddenly fail, the other one can take over. Additionally using both brakes diminish the stopping distance compared to breaking with just one break

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Is there a difference in the tendency of the wheels to lock?

options.text: Yes, as a rule, the rear wheel locks first
Yes, as a rule, the front wheel locks first
No, as a rule, both wheels lock at the same time

correct_answers.text: Yes, as a rule, the rear wheel locks first

comment: When breaking, more weight is applied on the front wheel and less on the back wheel. For this reason, the back wheel tends to lock first

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Is there a difference in the braking action?

options.text: Yes, as a rule the front wheel brake has greater braking action
Yes, as a rule the rear wheel brake has greater braking action
No, as a rule, both brakes have the same braking action

correct_answers.text: Yes, as a rule the front wheel brake has greater braking action

comment: When breaking, more weight is applied on the front wheel and less on the back wheel thus the front brake provides more braking power

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You come unexpectedly upon a stretch of road with loose chippings. What do you do?

options.text: Reduce speed cautiously
Avoid braking hard and leaning over
Apply the front brake only

correct_answers.text: Reduce speed cautiously
Avoid braking hard and leaning over

comment: Coming soon...

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Your vehicle was parked for a long time in the open in moist weather. What must you reckon with when applying the brakes for the first time?

options.text: The wheels have a dangerous tendency to lock
Reduced braking action
Reduced braking action of the engine

correct_answers.text: The wheels have a dangerous tendency to lock
Reduced braking action

comment: When wet, brakes are less effective and the wheels will have a tendency to lock more. It has however no impact on braking of the engine on a lower gear.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can be the reason for a motorized bicycle skidding on bends?

options.text: Heavy braking
Wet or icy road surface
Sand or loose chippings

correct_answers.text: Heavy braking
Wet or icy road surface
Sand or loose chippings

comment: Skidding risk is increases because of slippery surfaces such as wet road, ice, sand, dirt, leaves, cobblestones, manholes. It can also be created due to heavy braking.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: When does the braking distance increase?

options.text: When driving down slopes
When carrying heavy luggage
When there is headwind

correct_answers.text: When driving down slopes
When carrying heavy luggage

comment: The heavier the vehicle, the longer will be the braking distance. Downward slopes as well as slippery surfaces also increase the braking distance

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What particular characteristics of disc brakes must you remember when driving on a wet road surface?

options.text: As a rule, the effect of disc brakes starts later than on a dry road surface
As a rule, the effect of disc brakes starts earlier than on a dry road surface

correct_answers.text: As a rule, the effect of disc brakes starts later than on a dry road surface

comment: As a car driver you have to take into account that when the street is wet the effect of the disc brakes usually takes effect much later than on a dry road.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What increases the danger of "flying out" of a bend when driving at high speed?

options.text: Braking
Accelerating
Disengaging the clutch

correct_answers.text: Braking
Accelerating

comment: Decelerating or accelerating your car will result in less steering effort. As a result, there is an increased danger of "flying out" of the curve at high speed. Uncouple to get more steering power.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you take into consideration when checking tyre pressure?

options.text: Load/Number of passengers in the car
Tyre temperature
Material of the wheels (steel/aluminium)

correct_answers.text: Load/Number of passengers in the car
Tyre temperature

comment: When checking tire pressure, you must also take into account the temperature and load of the vehicle. These can influence the tire pressure. By contrast, the material of the wheel rim doesn't matter.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You drive round a bend once at 30 km/h and again at 60 km/h. How does the centrifugal force change?

options.text: - is four times as high
- is twice as high
- is the same

correct_answers.text: - is four times as high

comment: The centrifugal force quadruples when the speed is doubled, that is, when you take the curve at 60 km/h the second time.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What increases the effect of centrifugal force on the vehicle when driving round bends?

options.text: Higher speed
Smaller radius of a bend
Higher tyre pressure

correct_answers.text: Higher speed
Smaller radius of a bend

comment: The speed has an immediate effect on the level of centrifugal force. Your braking distance quadruples when you drive at twice the speed. The centrifugal force increases the smaller the curve radius. The tire pressure has no effect on the centrifugal force.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving a motorcycle with sidecar on the right. Which driving technique must you use on bends?

options.text: Moderate throttle on right-hand bends
Release throttle and brake lightly on left-hand bends
Always disengage the clutch on all bends

correct_answers.text: Moderate throttle on right-hand bends
Release throttle and brake lightly on left-hand bends

comment: Driving with a sidecar increase your weight, you thus need to go slower when turning

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Where should a passenger on a motorcycle with sidecar sit to reduce the risk of tipping over on bends?

options.text: In the sidecar
On the motorcycle
The position of the occupants has no significance

correct_answers.text: In the sidecar

comment: In order to keep a motorcycle with a sidecar stable, the weight should be equaly distributed on each side of the center of gravity. The second passenger therefore should sit in the sidecar

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can you do if the sidecar lifts off the ground on a right-hand bend when you are driving a motorcycle and sidecar (sidecar on the right)?

options.text: Release throttle, brake, shift your body weight to the right
Reduce steering lock angle, trace a wider arc within the lane you are travelling
Increase steering lock angle, accelerate

correct_answers.text: Release throttle, brake, shift your body weight to the right
Reduce steering lock angle, trace a wider arc within the lane you are travelling

comment: When turning right, a torque force will push the sidecar up. To reduce this torque you can slow down, shift your body weight to the right and make a wider turn.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can happen to a motorcycle with a sidecar attached on the right when driving too fast round a right-hand bend?

options.text: The sidecar lifts off the ground and the combination tips over
The motorcycle lifts off the ground and the combination tips over to the right

correct_answers.text: The sidecar lifts off the ground and the combination tips over

comment: When turning right, a torque force will push the sidecar up. At high speed the sidecar could be lifted-up, loose contact with the ground and tip over.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: So far, you have only driven solo motorcycles. You now change over to a combination (sidecar on the right, unbraked). How does driving differ?

options.text: When accelerating, the combination pulls to the right
When driving on bends, you must steer instead of leaning over
When braking, the combination pulls to the right

correct_answers.text: When accelerating, the combination pulls to the right
When driving on bends, you must steer instead of leaning over

comment: As the sidecar is attached to your right, you cannot lean right and need to steer instead. When accelerating the sidecar tends to be pulled to the right. When breaking the sidecar will be pulled to the left

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: So far, you have only driven solo motorcycles. You now change over to a combination (sidecar on the right, unbraked). What is different?

options.text: When braking, the combination pulls to the left
The sidecar may lift off the ground on right-hand bends
You must not drive with dipped headlights during daytime

correct_answers.text: When braking, the combination pulls to the left
The sidecar may lift off the ground on right-hand bends

comment: As the sidecar is attached to your right, you cannot lean right and need to steer instead. When turning right, a torque force will push your sidecar up. At high speed the sidecar could be lifted-up, loose contact with the ground and tip over. When accelerating the sidecar tends to be pulled to the right. When breaking the sidecar will be pulled to the left

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What should you know about using the emergency operation of bus doors?

options.text: - should enable anyone on the bus to open the doors following accidents and breakdowns
- if misused, can lead to the doors being opened when the bus is moving
- can only be released by the driver

correct_answers.text: - should enable anyone on the bus to open the doors following accidents and breakdowns
- if misused, can lead to the doors being opened when the bus is moving

comment: Coming soon...

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can happen if you accelerate very rapidly when moving off on your motorbike?

options.text: The passenger can fall off
The front lift can lift up from the road surface
I can lose control over the motorbike

correct_answers.text: The passenger can fall off
The front lift can lift up from the road surface
I can lose control over the motorbike

comment: Fast and sudden accelerations could lead to the front wheel lifting off the road, passenger falling and losing control overt the motorcycle as there is less or no steering due to less or no contact between the front wheel and the road

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving a local transport bus and want to drive away from a bus stop. What must you look out for?

options.text: - all doors are properly closed
- no persons are directly in front of the bus
- flowing traffic is not endangered

correct_answers.text: - all doors are properly closed
- no persons are directly in front of the bus
- flowing traffic is not endangered

comment: Coming soon...

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving in the wet in a car with trailer on a narrow rural road and are approaching a clearly visible but tight left-hand bend. What should you do?

options.text: I reduce my speed before the bend
I remain in the centre of the lane and only accelerate again once I am back on the straight
I only brake once I have reached the apex of the bend

correct_answers.text: I reduce my speed before the bend
I remain in the centre of the lane and only accelerate again once I am back on the straight

comment: Decrease your speed before the turn. Take the weather conditions into account. Keep in mind that the centrifugal force grows twice as fast as the speed. You should only accelerate again in the curve vertex.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What do you have to pay attention to, when jacking up a motorbike on its centre stand?

options.text: - can tip over even when just slightly tilted
- can be difficult to jack up when on a steep gradient
- is best jacked up from a seated position

correct_answers.text: - can tip over even when just slightly tilted
- can be difficult to jack up when on a steep gradient

comment: Setting a motorcycle on its centre stand requires more effort and can be difficult when on a steep slope. It is also sensitive to tipping over when tilted on the side

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What should you do if your motorbike starts to wobble?

options.text: - throttle back, disengage the clutch and brake carefully
- change down gears and accelerate as quickly as possible
- compensate wobbling by quickly counter-steering

correct_answers.text: - throttle back, disengage the clutch and brake carefully

comment: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, decelerate, disengage the clutch and brake. Do not accelerate as it might increase the wobble and lead to an accident. Also do not try to compensate it as it is dangerous and could also lead to an accident

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving a motorbike equipped with an anti-lock braking system (ABS). How do you perform an emergency braking manoeuvre?

options.text: Effect the best-possible deceleration using hand and foot brake
Do not press the foot brake lever, because the ABS only functions at the front
Operate the hand and foot brake lever intermittently ("intermittent braking")

correct_answers.text: Effect the best-possible deceleration using hand and foot brake

comment: Breaking both foot and hand brake will result in the shortest stopping distance. ABS improves the stopping distance by un-blocking the wheels during strong brakes

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: How can driver assistance systems be helpful?

options.text: In increasing road safety
In assisting the driver
To compensate for unfitness to drive

correct_answers.text: In increasing road safety
In assisting the driver

comment: Driver assistance systems assist the car driver and increase traffic safety when the navigation device is programmed before driving. However, driver assistance systems can not compensate for an unfitness to drive.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you be aware of, if you have to brake sharply while in a bend?

options.text: My motorcycle will become upright
I have to steer more strongly in order to maintain my cornering line
My cornering line decreases

correct_answers.text: My motorcycle will become upright
I have to steer more strongly in order to maintain my cornering line

comment: If you have to brake sharply in a curve, make sure that your motorcycle straightens up (inertia force). You have to turn harder to maintain the curve line.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you be aware of when driving a quad?

options.text: Wearing a suitable crash helmet is mandatory
Quads are prone to tipping over when driving through tight bends
The handling characteristics are similar to those of a car

correct_answers.text: Wearing a suitable crash helmet is mandatory
Quads are prone to tipping over when driving through tight bends

comment: Reduce speed when turning, as quads tend to tip over due to their high centre of gravity.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What should be observed when driving a quad?

options.text: Protective motorcycle clothing should be worn
A warning triangle must be carried on the quad
The necessary steering force can be significantly greater than with a car

correct_answers.text: Protective motorcycle clothing should be worn
A warning triangle must be carried on the quad
The necessary steering force can be significantly greater than with a car

comment: The quad has no steering assistance, so steering may be more difficult than driving a car.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving a motorbike with a manual gearbox. What do you have to do in order to be ready to brake?

options.text: I place my hand on the handbrake lever
I place my foot over the brake pedal
I change up to a higher gear

correct_answers.text: I place my hand on the handbrake lever
I place my foot over the brake pedal

comment: Put your foot and hand already over the brake levers to initiate the braking process more quickly.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You want to use a carrying case or pannier affixed to the side of your motorcycle. What must you be especially aware of?

options.text: An unequal distribution of weight should be avoided
Heavier pieces of luggage should be stowed as close to the bottom as possible
The gross vehicle weight rating of the motorcycle may not be exceeded

correct_answers.text: An unequal distribution of weight should be avoided
Heavier pieces of luggage should be stowed as close to the bottom as possible
The gross vehicle weight rating of the motorcycle may not be exceeded

comment: Make sure that the weight is evenly distributed to stabilise the driving behaviour. Stow heavy luggage as far down as possible to keep the centre of gravity as low as possible.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Your motorbike is equipped with a traction control system (TCS). What is the system designed to do?

options.text: - prevents the rear wheel spinning when moving off
- stabilises the motorbike during an emergency braking manoeuvre
- prevents the front wheel from locking during braking

correct_answers.text: - prevents the rear wheel spinning when moving off

comment: Slippage" is the sudden increase in the speed of a drive wheel when it loses grip because you have accelerated too much. This triggers the anti-slip control, which prevents the wheel from spinning by braking.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving around a bend in the road, and the turning radius becomes smaller as the bend progresses. You had reckoned that the turning radius would be larger. How must you now react?

options.text: I increase my inclined position
I reduce my speed
I activate the emergency stop switch

correct_answers.text: I increase my inclined position
I reduce my speed

comment:
If you have estimated the cornering radius to be larger, you should reduce your speed; by reducing your speed, you can drive a smaller cornering radius. 
You can also increase the lean angle in the bend so that you can take tighter bends.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What should you take into account when you have to brake unexpectedly sharply while driving around a road bend?

options.text: My motorcycle tends to drive straight ahead
I should counter-steer gently
The driving line of my motorcycle remains unchanged

correct_answers.text: My motorcycle tends to drive straight ahead
I should counter-steer gently

comment: When you brake in a bend, your motorbike is lifted up by the force of inertia. You have to counteract this by counter-steering with feeling. Otherwise you will continue straight ahead and not make the bend.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: In bends with poor road conditions, what increases the risk of skidding?

options.text: Having a damaged chassis
Having the wrong tyre inflation pressure
Having a wrongly loaded cargo

correct_answers.text: Having a damaged chassis
Having the wrong tyre inflation pressure
Having a wrongly loaded cargo

comment:
Ideally, all wheels should press on the road with the same force to ensure optimum grip and handling. If this is not the case, it can increase the risk of skidding in poor road conditions.
The suspension, for example, has the task of keeping all tyres on the road with the same force. If the suspension is damaged, it can no longer do this. The risk of skidding also increases if the tyre pressure is incorrect or if the vehicle is incorrectly or unevenly loaded.
This is because the tyres cannot apply the same force to the road and you lose grip more quickly.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are travelling along a winding road with a steep gradient. Your motorbike is fully loaded. What is the right course of action?

options.text: I drive in a low gear in order to use my engine’s braking action
I avoid accelerating to high speeds between bends in the road
I brake using the front-wheel brake only

correct_answers.text: I drive in a low gear in order to use my engine’s braking action
I avoid accelerating to high speeds between bends in the road

comment:
Avoid speeding up between bends, because speeding up would put even more strain on the brakes. Therefore, ride downhill without speeding up. 
Use the front and rear brakes evenly and try to use the braking effect of the motor to relieve the brakes. The higher the engine speed, the greater the braking effect.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: When is there a risk that the front wheel of the motorbike will lose contact with the carriageway?

options.text: - accelerate in a low gear
- accelerate while carrying a pillion passenger
- brake using the front-wheel brake

correct_answers.text: - accelerate in a low gear
- accelerate while carrying a pillion passenger

comment:
When speeding up, the weight shifts to the back. Extreme speeding in a low gear shifts the centre of gravity behind the rear axle and the front wheel lifts off.
A passenger also shifts the weight to the rear when speeding up. This weight shift relieves the front wheel and can cause it to lift off.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What might happen if you shift to a low gear while travelling at a high speed?

options.text: The rear wheel may lock
There is a high risk of crashing to the ground
The front wheel may lift up from the road surface

correct_answers.text: The rear wheel may lock
There is a high risk of crashing to the ground

comment: The sudden, rapid increase in engine speed when engaging the clutch creates a braking effect. The engine braking force can cause your rear wheel to lock up or slip and lose grip on the road. You could lose control of your motorbike and crash.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: How should you respond if your motorbike begins to wobble?

options.text: - immediately release the accelerator and slow down
- avoid high speeds as I continue my journey
- counter-steer right now

correct_answers.text: - immediately release the accelerator and slow down
- avoid high speeds as I continue my journey

comment: By reducing the speed immediately, you can reduce swaying and increase driving stability. Swaying occurs at high speeds. So avoid driving very fast when continuing your journey.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What is the purpose of an emergency stop switch on a motorbike?

options.text: - turns off the engine
- turns off the lights
- triggers the eCall system

correct_answers.text: - turns off the engine

comment: The emergency stop switch switches off the engine. You can use it to switch off the engine quickly in dangerous situations without having to turn the key.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What applies to the effectiveness of the front and rear wheel brakes, especially at higher speeds?

options.text: - of the front brake is larger
- of the rear wheel brake is larger
- of the front and rear wheel brakes are equally powerful

correct_answers.text: - of the front brake is larger

comment: When braking, the weight shifts forward, which puts greater strain on the front wheel. That's why the front wheel brake is usually designed for higher braking effects in order to make the greater load easier to control.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can cause a motorcycle to oscillate at high speed?

options.text: - with unbalanced wheels
- on uneven road surfaces
- with heavy luggage at the rear

correct_answers.text: - with unbalanced wheels
- on uneven road surfaces
- with heavy luggage at the rear

comment:
At high speeds on uneven roads or if the wheels are not balanced, your motorcycle tends to "sway" more quickly because the unevenness changes the road's position.
If you have a heavy load on the rear of your motorcycle, there will be less weight on the front wheel. At high speeds, your motorcycle may sway, making it harder for you to control your motorcycle.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What changes when a caravan trailer is towed?

options.text: The distance for overtaking increases considerably
Hasty movements of the steering wheel increase the danger of skidding
The braking distance is reduced considerably

correct_answers.text: The distance for overtaking increases considerably
Hasty movements of the steering wheel increase the danger of skidding

comment: If you drive with a caravan, not only does it increase the risk of skidding, the overtaking and braking distances will be longer as well. This is due to the additional load to be pulled and the pulling motion of the trailer.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What changes in a car when towing a two-axle trailer?

options.text: More space is needed when turning and driving round bends
Acceleration capacity is reduced
Driving stability increases

correct_answers.text: More space is needed when turning and driving round bends
Acceleration capacity is reduced

comment: The combination of car and trailer requires more space when driving on bends and when turning. Likewise, the mass changes the accelerating ability. It is decreasing significantly.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are in your car towing a trailer on a road with oncoming traffic and want to turn left. What must you particularly remember when you set off again?

options.text: Think about the length of your car and trailer combination
Consider the reduced acceleration capacity
Warn oncoming traffic by flashing your lights

correct_answers.text: Think about the length of your car and trailer combination
Consider the reduced acceleration capacity

comment: With a trailer you have a lower accelerating ability, changed mass and a greater total length. This must be taken into consideration when you're starting your car again. Oncoming traffic must not be warned in this case by using the flash light.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are in your car towing a trailer which has no brakes and you approach a long steep downhill slope. What is correct?

options.text: Reduce speed, if necessary, engage low gear in time, be ready to brake
Make allowance for the pushing effect of the trailer
Relieve the car brakes by disengaging the clutch at frequent intervals

correct_answers.text: Reduce speed, if necessary, engage low gear in time, be ready to brake
Make allowance for the pushing effect of the trailer

comment: Reduce your speed on time. Us a gear as low as possible. The thus activated engine brake supports the braking action of the pedal braking. By no means you should put your car in idling. This would make the vehicle faster.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you check on a car with a caravan trailer before setting out on a journey?

options.text: Whether the lights of the trailer are working
Whether the view through the rear-view mirrors is adequate
Whether the passengers in the caravan trailer have put on their safety belts

correct_answers.text: Whether the lights of the trailer are working
Whether the view through the rear-view mirrors is adequate

comment: Caravans restrict the view to the back. Therefore, you must check before the start of the journey, if the mirrors provide sufficient visibility to the back. You also need to make sure that the illuminating devices are working.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are in your car towing a fully loaded trailer which has no brakes. What is correct?

options.text: Braking distance increases
Reaction distance increases
Stopping distance reduces

correct_answers.text: Braking distance increases

comment: Note that a fully loaded trailer without its own brake extends the braking distance and thus the stopping distance by the respective trailer load. The thinking distance does not change in this case.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You want to tow a singe-axle caravan trailer behind your car. What must you check?

options.text: If the permissible trailer load or the permissible coupling of the car are exceeded
If additional rear-view mirrors must be mounted because of the width of the trailer
If the trailer is licensed to transport passengers

correct_answers.text: If the permissible trailer load or the permissible coupling of the car are exceeded
If additional rear-view mirrors must be mounted because of the width of the trailer

comment: The caravan reduces the view to the back. You as a car driver have to check whether the rear view through the existing mirrors is sufficient. You may need to attach extra mirrors to your car. Towing vehicle and trailer must always be coordinated.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You want to set off in an automatic car (hydraulic converter). What must you know?

options.text: When selecting a gear, the car must, as a rule, be held by the service brakes
The selector lever must only be moved when the engine has stopped
The engine revolutions must be raised considerably so that the engine does not stall

correct_answers.text: When selecting a gear, the car must, as a rule, be held by the service brakes

comment: If you give a "go" with an engaged gear as a car driver in a vehicle with automatic transmission it will try to start driving. This can only be prevented by operating the service brake. The selector lever can and may be operated with the engine stationary and running.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you remember with regard to tyre pressure?

options.text: To check the air pressure regularly, including that of the spare wheel
To increase the pressure to the level stated in the vehicle manual when the vehicle is heavily loaded
To reduce the air pressure before longer trips

correct_answers.text: To check the air pressure regularly, including that of the spare wheel
To increase the pressure to the level stated in the vehicle manual when the vehicle is heavily loaded

comment: By regularly checking the air pressure of the tires, tire damage can be avoided, but fuel can also be saved. If you put your vehicle under a greater burden, you need to adjust the tire pressure.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You had a tyre failure and must mount the emergency wheel. What is prohibited when you continue to drive?

options.text: Driving faster than 80 km/h
Driving longer than necessary with the emergency wheel
Taking passengers

correct_answers.text: Driving faster than 80 km/h
Driving longer than necessary with the emergency wheel

comment: Emergency wheels have a different design than conventional wheels and are only allowed up to a speed of 80 km/h. They have worse operating characteristics. You should only drive with them as far as necessary. Taking other people with you is allowed.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: When driving, you notice that the car constantly pulls to the left. What could be the cause of this?

options.text: Too little air in the front left tyre
Incorrect wheel adjustment at the front axle (track, wheel camber)
The left rear tyre is extensively worn

correct_answers.text: Too little air in the front left tyre
Incorrect wheel adjustment at the front axle (track, wheel camber)

comment: If your vehicle pulls to the left so that countersteering is required, too little air pressure in the left tire could be the cause or a different wheel setting. A badly worn tire usually does not have this effect.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What does a front-wheel drive car tend to do if you accelerate too much on a bend?

options.text: The front end tends to turn out to the side
The vehicle tends to oversteer
The rear end tends to turn out to the side

correct_answers.text: The front end tends to turn out to the side

comment: As a car driver, you must always expect your vehicle with front-wheel drive to swing off in front if you over-accelerate on a turn. Your vehicle will more likely under than oversteer.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What does a rear-wheel drive car tend to do if you accelerate too much on a bend?

options.text: The rear end tends to turn out to the side
The front end tends to turn out to the side
The car tends to understeer

correct_answers.text: The rear end tends to turn out to the side

comment: You should always expect your vehicle with rear wheel drive to swing off to the back if you over-accelerate on a turn. It is more likely to oversteer than understeer.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What are the advantages of an anti-slip device (ASR)?

options.text: No wheelspin when setting off
Reduced danger of sliding sideways when setting off on a slippery roadway
No locking of the wheels when braking

correct_answers.text: No wheelspin when setting off
Reduced danger of sliding sideways when setting off on a slippery roadway

comment: The traction control system (TCS) of a car prevents the wheels of the vehicle from spinning, especially when accelerating faster. Slipping away to the side when starting to drive on slippery roads is thereby largely prevented.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You want to couple up a trailer with ball coupling. What is correct?

options.text: The claw of the coupling must fit securely around the ball. The locking device must engage
The electrics must be connected
The jack wheel must be set so that it can also run when driving

correct_answers.text: The claw of the coupling must fit securely around the ball. The locking device must engage
The electrics must be connected

comment: In a trailer with ball clutch, the clutch dog must firmly enclose the spherical head. The fuse must engage. Make sure the electrical connection works. The support wheel must not run while driving. It must be locked in high position.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you do after coupling up a single-axle trailer with overrun brakes?

options.text: Check that the brakes are working
Raise the jack wheel, if fitted, to the highest setting
Attach the brakeaway cable to the coupling of the motor vehicle

correct_answers.text: Check that the brakes are working
Raise the jack wheel, if fitted, to the highest setting
Attach the brakeaway cable to the coupling of the motor vehicle

comment: The breakaway cable must be hung on the coupling device of the towing vehicle. With an overrun brake, the trailer brakes automatically when the connection to the towing vehicle breaks off. The function of the brake must be checked. The support wheel must not run while driving, so it should be brought to the upper position.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you bear in mind when loading a single-axle trailer?

options.text: - axle load
- load on the coupling
- total mass

correct_answers.text: - axle load
- load on the coupling
- total mass

comment: When loading a single-axle trailer, you must ensure to comply with the total mass and that your load does not exceed the permissible axial load and bearing load.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You want to park your single-axle trailer (overrun brakes, 1000 kg permissible total mass) on a slope. What must you do?

options.text: Pull the parking brake
Place wheel chocks under the wheels
Engage the reverse lock

correct_answers.text: Pull the parking brake
Place wheel chocks under the wheels

comment: You must always secure your trailer against possibly rolling away. To do this, you must use the parking brake and place the wheel chocks in front of the wheels. Usually such trailers have no reverse lockout.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Which dangerous defects can have occurred on a trailer with overrun brakes which has been parked for some time?

options.text: The brakes may not work because of rust
Cable connections can be defective
Tyre pressure may have increased greatly due to exposure to the sun

correct_answers.text: The brakes may not work because of rust
Cable connections can be defective

comment: If you leave a trailer standing somewhere for a long time, the weather can cause damage: electrical connections can be damaged, rust can form on the brakes. Sun exposure does not increase the tire pressure too much, so that no dangerous defects occur.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What must you remember when loading a trailer?

options.text: - must be securely packed
- must not project more than 1 m beyond the rear reflectors, unless specially marked
- must not project more than 1 m beyond the front of the towing vehicle

correct_answers.text: - must be securely packed
- must not project more than 1 m beyond the rear reflectors, unless specially marked

comment: Always pay attention to the proper securing of your cargo. In order not to endanger yourself and other road users, you must always have a clear view and full control over your vehicle. The cargo must be marked at the rear and may not protrude more than 50 cm at the front.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Why should you not press the clutch and switch off the engine at the same time when driving down a long slope?

options.text: The steering of vehicles with servo-assisted steering immediately becomes unusually heavy
Full braking power cannot be reached in vehicles with brake booster system despite great force being applied to the pedal
The battery will be overcharged

correct_answers.text: The steering of vehicles with servo-assisted steering immediately becomes unusually heavy
Full braking power cannot be reached in vehicles with brake booster system despite great force being applied to the pedal

comment: When the engine is off, the engine brake (brake booster) cannot work. Even power steering is not turned on then. To respond quickly and effectively to dangerous situations, you may need both.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Why should you not apply the clutch when driving on a long, steep downhill slope?

options.text: Because the braking action of the engine will have no effect
Because this causes unnecessary wear of the brakes
Because in this case the brake servo unit will no longer function

correct_answers.text: Because the braking action of the engine will have no effect
Because this causes unnecessary wear of the brakes

comment: If you step down the clutch, the engine brake will not work and you will have to use the service brake more. As a result, overheating and increased brake wear can occur.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What is correct when coupling a full trailer?

options.text: - should be positioned in the driver's line of vision and guide him
- warns of obstacles and road users not visible to the driver
- hold the drawbar until it has locked into the hitch

correct_answers.text: - should be positioned in the driver's line of vision and guide him
- warns of obstacles and road users not visible to the driver

comment: You should make sure that a suitable person in the viewing area is about you and instructor you and that this person obstacles and road users that you can not see, warns you of a Mehrachsanhängers when coupling.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving in a pair with a load. What should be noted when performing an emergency stop?

options.text: - have to apply more braking force
- that the rear-wheel brakes may operate more powerfully
- have to apply less braking force

correct_answers.text: - have to apply more braking force
- that the rear-wheel brakes may operate more powerfully

comment: If you are driving with more weight, you should apply more braking force. Due to the additional weight, the rear wheel brakes will brake more as well

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You suddenly have to brake when cornering on a wet carriageway. What special aspects exist with a vehicle equipped with an anti-lock braking system (ABS)?

options.text: The steering capability is retained for longer
The vehicle will always remain stable
It is not possible for the vehicle to skid out of the bend

correct_answers.text: The steering capability is retained for longer

comment: On wet roads, the antilocking system prevents the wheels from locking and shortens the braking distance. In addition, the vehicle remains more steerable when braking. On gravel or snow, the braking distance can certainly be much longer.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What is the effect of the cornering characteristics of a combination vehicle (car towing a caravan) when taking a turn?

options.text: - can jut out
- can cut the corner
- generally follows the track of the car

correct_answers.text: - can jut out
- can cut the corner

comment: Despite careful driving, it is possible that the trailer cuts the curve or even swings out. The car driver must therefore proceed with caution in order to exclude hazards to others.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You experience pendular movements on your motorbike. What could be the cause of these?

options.text: The load
A wheel imbalance
Driving at low revs

correct_answers.text: The load
A wheel imbalance

comment: If your entire motorcycle swings to the front and back, this could be caused by heavy load or imbalance in the wheel

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can restrict the functionality of a lane departure warning system?

options.text: A dirty road surface
The absence of road markings
The absence of guardrails

correct_answers.text: A dirty road surface
The absence of road markings

comment: The function of the lane departure warning system may be limited if the system cannot properly pick up lane signals. This is, because the computer-controlled system works on the basis of different optical systems. There are no signals from the guardrails. Another name for the lane departure warning system is: Lane Keeping Assist (active lane departure warning system with steering assistance).

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What information should you obtain before undertaking a journey with a purely electric vehicle?

options.text: The locations at which I can charge the vehicle
What I have to do following an accident
Factors that influence the range

correct_answers.text: The locations at which I can charge the vehicle
What I have to do following an accident
Factors that influence the range

comment: The car driver should inform himself about the range of the electric vehicle before starting the journey. This differs significantly from the range of conventional vehicles and more frequent stops to recharge the batteries are necessary. You should also take into account that there is more technology in an electric vehicle. Although it is generally true that electric vehicles are just as safe as conventional cars. But in their bodies usually run cables that are designed for enormously high voltages.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are planning a longer journey with a purely electric vehicle. What should you be aware of?

options.text: The availability of electric charging stations
The battery charging time
The influence of external ambient temperatures on the range

correct_answers.text: The availability of electric charging stations
The battery charging time
The influence of external ambient temperatures on the range

comment: If you are planning a longer journey with a purely electric vehicle, you should consider that your car has a much lower range compared to conventional vehicles. In addition, the capacity of the batteries is influenced by the outside temperature.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What should you be aware of when charging purely electric vehicles?

options.text: The charge time depends on the power supply
Charging should only be performed with a charging cable approved by the manufacturer
Charging is available at every filling station

correct_answers.text: The charge time depends on the power supply
Charging should only be performed with a charging cable approved by the manufacturer

comment: When charging pure electric vehicles, you must be aware that they cannot be recharged at every gas station. Only use the charging cables approved by the manufacturer. Depending on the power connection, the charging time varies.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: How is a purely electric vehicle different from a vehicle with a combustion engine?

options.text: - have a lower engine noise
- do not have any direct exhaust emissions
- have a lower aerodynamic drag

correct_answers.text: - have a lower engine noise
- do not have any direct exhaust emissions

comment: Pure electric vehicles are almost noiseless. These vehicles also have no direct exhaust emissions. The aerodynamic drag depends on the volume of the body and not on the type of drive.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving a purely electric vehicle in a residential area. What should you be aware of due to your lower engine noise?

options.text: Pedestrians will not notice me or will do so later than usual
Cyclist travelling ahead will turn left, without looking behind them
Vehicles following behind will tailgate me

correct_answers.text: Pedestrians will not notice me or will do so later than usual
Cyclist travelling ahead will turn left, without looking behind them

comment: With a pure electric vehicle, you are almost noiseless on the road and you can acoustically be hardly perceived by other road users. Especially cyclists are at risk if they hear no engine noise. Without looking back, they often turn.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving a motor vehicle fitted with anti-lock braking system (ABS). How do you achieve the shortest possible braking distance?

options.text: - suddenly and with maximum force
- carefully and then increasingly harder
- multiple times at quick intervals and with maximum force

correct_answers.text: - suddenly and with maximum force

comment: If you drive a car with an automatic anti-lock braking system, you achieve the shortest braking distance by braking abruptly and with maximum pedal force. The ABS prevents the wheels from locking during braking.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: A lane assist system with corrective steer control can help you when driving. What should you be aware of?

options.text: - keep the vehicle in lane if the road markings are clear
- not function if the road markings are poor
- compensate for a lack of fitness to drive (e.g. tiredness)

correct_answers.text: - keep the vehicle in lane if the road markings are clear
- not function if the road markings are poor

comment: A prerequisite for a perfect function of the lane departure warning system are good road markings. Keep in mind that technical driving assistants cannot compensate for inability to drive. As a car driver, you must be able to intervene into the driving experience at all times.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: You are driving at high speed into a bend. What could happen if you had to brake suddenly?

options.text: - could lose its grip on the road
- could skid out of the bend
- will constantly maintain its driving stability with the stability control

correct_answers.text: - could lose its grip on the road
- could skid out of the bend

comment: If you drive fast into a tight curve, you lose road grip when you brake hard and slide out of the curve. (Centrifugal force)

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can result in your motor vehicle skidding while driving round a bend?

options.text: Heavy oversteer
Driving too fast
Gently accelerating at the exit of the bend

correct_answers.text: Heavy oversteer
Driving too fast

comment: If you turn sharply, your vehicle may start to skid on bends. This can also happen if you drive too fast. Adjust your speed when cornering.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: The lane keeping assist system warns you with acoustic, haptic or optical signals. What might be the cause of this?

options.text: My vehicle is getting close to the road markings at the side of the road
My vehicle is undercutting the safety distance to the vehicle ahead
Another vehicle is overtaking me with not enough side clearance

correct_answers.text: My vehicle is getting close to the road markings at the side of the road

comment: If you drift out of your lane, the lane departure warning system detects this by recognising that you are approaching the lane marking. The permissible total mass must not be exceeded.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: In what situation can the lane keep assist system with steering override help you?

options.text: - on motorways
- on rural roads
- in constricted roadworks sites with poor road markings

correct_answers.text: - on motorways
- on rural roads

comment:
On motorways and country roads, steering intervention by the lane departure warning system can be helpful, as the markings are clearly visible there.
Due to poor markings and narrow lanes in roadworks, steering intervention by the lane departure warning system is not possible as it will most likely not be detected correctly.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: With which driving task can the lane keep assist system with steering override help the driver?

options.text: When driving in a straight line
When turning
When overtaking

correct_answers.text: When driving in a straight line

comment:
If the lane markings are good, Lane Keeping Assist with steering intervention can help you to keep the vehicle on the lane when driving straight ahead.
When turning, you cross lanes and markings; the lane departure warning system cannot intervene to support you here. When overtaking, you signal to the lane departure warning system by flashing that you are crossing the lane markings intentionally. Thus, it does not intervene during the overtaking process.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can negatively affect the functioning of the lane keep assist system?

options.text: The weather conditions
The condition of the road markings
Additional road markings within a roadworks site

correct_answers.text: The weather conditions
The condition of the road markings
Additional road markings within a roadworks site

comment:
If the lane markings are in a poor condition, the lane keeping assistant cannot recognise where the lane to be maintained is. Due to additional lane markings in construction areas, it is not obvious which is the lane to be kept to.
Weather conditions can affect the sensors of the lane departure warning system. In addition, water or snow can distort the markings.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Under what conditions will the lane keep assist system with steering override function optimally?

options.text: Where there are clear road markings
Where there are patches of snow on the road surface
Where there are additional roadworks markings

correct_answers.text: Where there are clear road markings

comment:
The lane keeping assistant works best with clear lane markings. 
Poor or additional markings in roadworks will not allow the lane departure warning system to intervene, as it will most likely not be detected correctly.
Weather conditions can affect the sensors of the lane departure warning system. In addition, snow can distort the markings.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What driver assistance system offers a high degree of road safety potential?

options.text: The brake assist
The autonomous emergency brake
The cruise control system

correct_answers.text: The brake assist
The autonomous emergency brake

comment:
The Autonomous Emergency Brake Assist constantly detects the traffic in front of the vehicle. If a hazard is imminent, the Emergency Brake Assist can carry out an emergency braking manoeuvre. 
Braking too late or too timidly are often causes of traffic accidents. Brake assistants usually react faster than humans and thus offer more safety.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: How can driver assistance systems help you?

options.text: - warn me of danger
- help me perform driving tasks
- intervene automatically in critical road traffic situations

correct_answers.text: - warn me of danger
- help me perform driving tasks
- intervene automatically in critical road traffic situations

comment:
In critical traffic situations, driver assistance systems can react quickly and intervene automatically by steering or braking etc..
If danger is imminent, they can warn you with light, sound and haptic signals. Driver assistance systems can also help you with driving tasks, such as keeping in lane.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: What can result if you accelerate too hard when driving a front-wheel drive car through a road bend?

options.text: - The front of the car can swerve
- Steerability can be reduced
- The rear of the car can swerve

correct_answers.text: - The front of the car can swerve
- Steerability can be reduced

comment: If you give a front-wheel drive car too much gas in a bend, it can swerve over the front axle. The front tyres lose their grip on the road and your vehicle can no longer be steered, but continues straight ahead and breaks away.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
question_text: Under what conditions can an active lane change assist system perform a lane change?

options.text: - has detected an adequately marked carriageway with multiple lanes
- has not detected any vehicles in the relevant safety zone
- has detected a sufficiently large gap in the oncoming traffic

correct_answers.text: - has detected an adequately marked carriageway with multiple lanes
- has not detected any vehicles in the relevant safety zone

comment: The Active Lane Change Assistant only performs a lane change when it cannot detect any vehicle in the relevant safety zone. For an active lane change, the assistant must first detect a marked lane with several lanes.

chapter_name: Driving Operation Driving Physics Driving Technique
